_ext: keys below are pipeline extensions, additive to SPEC §4
protagonist: Dara Voss, full-time NYC app-based e-bike delivery courier -- a former claims-office data-entry clerk who keeps every week's numbers on a laminated, Sharpie-covered index card zip-tied to her handlebars, and who has just been accepted into a 21-month paralegal certificate program that fixes, for the first time, exactly how long she plans to keep riding

deliverables.text: A weekly cost-function derivation: using Appendix A's itemized rate components, write each option's total cost as a function of weeks, w, in simplified slope-intercept form, showing the distributive-property step and any like-terms combination.
A break-even system: set the two cost functions equal as a system of two linear equations and solve algebraically for the break-even number of weeks, rounding to a sensible whole number.

A net-savings x-intercept: define the net-savings function as B minus A, simplify to one weekly term, solve algebraically for its x-intercept, and explain what the x-intercept and y-intercept represent.
A distractor read: from Appendix B's graphed Whizz plan, identify its slope and y-intercept, write its linear equation, and explain why this plan is not relevant to Dara's actual decision.
A graph of both real options: graph Option A's and Option B's cost functions on one set of labeled axes for w = 0 to at least 130 weeks, marking the break-even intersection point.
A total-cost-at-horizon comparison: evaluate both cost functions at Dara's 91-week horizon, find the dollar difference, convert it to a percent margin, and recommend an option.

How To… Math Questions To Research

balance.argument_a: The Ownership Path costs Dara only her electricity (well under a dollar a week) plus a scaled-up self-maintenance estimate ($17.31/week) after the one-time $2,299.00 purchase -- a weekly rate roughly 46% of Zoomo's. Every week past the algebraic break-even point (about 106 weeks), Ownership is strictly cheaper, and it stays that way for as long as Dara keeps the bike after her 21-month program ends -- The Subscription Path has no such payoff, and every dollar paid to Zoomo is gone the moment the week ends.
balance.argument_b: The Subscription Path costs Dara nothing up front and covers every repair, no matter what breaks or when -- a real risk transfer The Ownership Path doesn't offer a new owner. At Dara's actual, fixed 91-week horizon, Subscription's total cost ($3,638.72) is lower than Ownership's ($3,963.72) by $325.00, about 8.2% -- because 91 weeks falls about 15 weeks short of the roughly 106-week break-even point, so Dara would sell (or simply stop needing) an owned bike before it ever earns back its own purchase price.
balance.margin_basis: Evaluate both cost functions C_A(w) and C_B(w) at w = 91 weeks (Dara's stated decision horizon), find the dollar difference, and express it as a percent of the more expensive option's total.

sensitivity_note: SPEC §6: the A-vs-B margin (8.20% at the base 91-week horizon) is sensitive to MA4's decision-horizon assumption and, nearly as much, MA3's annual-maintenance assumption -- see sensitivity_model.py FLEX = ["decision_horizon_weeks", "annual_maintenance_cost", "charging_range_low_mi"]. subscription_weekly_rate ($39.00, S1) and the purchase price ($2,299.00, S2) are deliberately excluded from FLEX -- they are cited figures, not stated assumptions; P6 (data decay), not P5, is the right probe for them. A +50% swing on decision_horizon_weeks (to 136.5 weeks) flips the winner to A at a 12.13% margin; a -50% swing (to 45.5 weeks) keeps B winning but pushes the margin to 41.90%, over the SPEC §2 20% cap. A -50% swing on annual_maintenance_cost flips the winner to A at 12.71%; a +50% swing keeps B winning but pushes the margin to 23.42%, also over the cap. charging_range_low_mi swings the margin by well under one percentage point in either direction and never flips or breaches the cap.

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: MA4's 91-week decision horizon has no public source -- it is Dara's own stated plan (the length of her certificate program). A +50% swing (136.5 weeks) flips the recommended option from B to A; a -50% swing (45.5 weeks) pushes the margin to 41.90%, well over the SPEC §2 20% cap. Disclosed here, in Appendix C's MA4 row, and in FACILITATOR.md's sensitivity note and Q1/Q5 -- not eliminated.

MA3's $900/year self-maintenance estimate has no public source at Dara's actual mileage -- it is a documented upward extrapolation from a cited commuter-mileage figure. A -50% swing flips the recommended option from B to A (12.71% margin); a +50% swing keeps B winning but pushes the margin to 23.42%, over the 20% cap. Disclosed here, in Appendix C's MA3 row, and in FACILITATOR.md's sensitivity note and Q2/Q5 -- not eliminated.
